' Instant February^ should bfe taken into Consideration

bn Thursday the 7th Day of March next; and that the several Petitions complaining of an undue Election and Retufn for the Borough of now appointed

for Tuesday the 5th Day of March next, and also, the Several Petitions complaining of an undue Election and Return for the Borough of Poole, now appointed for Thursday the 7th Day of March next, should be taken into Consideration on Tuesday the 12th Day of March next, before the Consideration of the Petition complaining of the Pontefract Election now appointed for that Day.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That on the above recited Days now appointed for the Consideration of the several Petitions above named; viz. on Thursday the 7th Day of March next, and on Tuesday the 12th Day of March next, or on any other Day in this Session of Parliament, on which any of the above-named Petitions shall he ordered to be taken into Consideration, and the House shall have proceeded to the Appointment of a Select Committee, for the Trial of any of the above-named Petitions, and the Names of the Members shall be drawn and called for that Purpose, Mr. Speaker should direct the Name of every Member so called, who shall be absent from the House, to be set aside; and that a List should be made of the Names of such absent Members to be reported, by Mr. Speaker, to the House on the next Sitting Day.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, upon the Report of the List of the Names of such absent Members, the Members, for whose Non-attendance, on the Appointment of any such Select Committee, a sufficient Excuse shall not be made and allowed by the House, should be forthwith ordered to be taken into the Custody of the Serjeant at Arms attending this House, and should not be discharged out of Custody without the special Order of the House.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the House should require, that strict Proof should be given of the Facts and Circumstances which shall be alleaged in Excuse for the Non-attendance of any Member, on the Appointment of any such Select Committee, as is above described.

The First Resolution of the Committee being read a Second Time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House, Nemine Contradicente.

A Motion Was made, and the Question being pro- Motion posed, 'J'hat the uniform and persevering Opposition respecting given by our Ancestors to every Attempt to erect Barracks in this Country, was founded upon a just Understanding of the true Principles of our free and excellent Constitution; and that this Opposition has been justified and supported by high Political and Legal Authority, whose recorded Opinion is, " That in Time of Peace " the Soldier should live intermixed with the People,

A Petition of Doctor Cuthbert Gordon, together with Copies of certain Certificates and Testimonials, &c. &c. thereunto annexed, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That in 1785, the

Petitioner submitted, under a certain specific Sum, his Discoveries in the Art of Dying in a Petition to this House, who, after referring it to a Committee, were pleased to address His Majesty in July 1786, and, in Consequence thereof, His Majesty was graciously pleased to appoint the Investigation of those Discoveries to the Right honourable the Lords of the Committee of Council for Trade, and the Petitioner submitted to their Lordships various Documents, on the small Scale of Dying, demonstrative of the Value and

Utility of his Discoveries, but their Lordships, not comprehending the Utility and Value of those Discoveries by the small Scale, ordered that Mr. Chamberlain Goodwin, of London, with the Assistance of the Society of Arts and Manufactures, should be desired to make the Experiment of dying One or Two Pieces of Cloth, or any other Woollen Manufacture on which the Experiment could be made, in Drab Colours or Black, in the Manner proposed by the Petitioner, in order to ascertain the Expence thereof, comparing it with the present Charge of dying Drabs, or of dying ordinary Blacks, or of dying the best Blacks on the Foundation of deep Blue, in the Manner at present practised, and also that the Petitioner should be authorized to hire One or Two Acres of Land, for the Cultivation of the Plant from which he draws his Red Colours, in order to ascertain to what Degree the said Plant can be improved, and what the Expence of Cultivation, and, that Mr. Charles Taylor, of Manchester, should be desired to dye some Cotton with the before-mentioned Plant, in order to determine what Species of Red would be produced thereby upon Cotton, and the Merit and Utility of that Manner of Dying, and, in the mean Time, their Lordships recommend to the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's Treasury, to give the Petitioner the Sum of £. 200, as a Reward for his Merit in discovering Substances useful in Dying, and as an Encouragement to proceed in the said Discoveries; and that the Petitioner, desirous to the utmost of his Abilities to afford the Committee of Council all the Satisfaction in his Power, applied to Messrs. Gooduin and Taylor to make the Experiments required in their Lordships Minutes; and the Society of Arts and Manufactures nominated Mr. William De-sanges to attend and assist Mr. Goodwin in the Experiments on Woollen Goods; but both Mr. Goodwin and Taylor, by their Letters to the Lords of the Committee, declined to make such Experiments, and the Petitioner had therefore Recourse to Mr. Desanges, nominated by the Society of Arts and Manufactures, and to Mr. Jacob Mills, an eminent practical Dyer in London, with respect to the Experiments to be made on Woollen Goods, and to Mr. Henry Gardiner, an eminent Callico Printer, at Wandsworth, in Surrey, with respect to Cottons, who recommended to Mr. George Milne, the Person who directs, and under whose Eye all the Experiments of the Printfield are performed, to see it properly investigated, and to certify accordingly (the Certificates and Testimonials of which said Messrs. William Desanges and Jacob Mills, and also of the said Mr. George Milne, are annexed to the Peti-tition); and that the Petitioner hath, in Conformity, as he apprehends, to the said Recommendation of their Lordships of the Committee of Council, proceeded in further ascertaining the Practicability of his said Discoveries, and for that Purpose has, at a very considerable Expence of Time and Money, exhibited in the Manufacturing Parts of Yorkshire and Lancashire, and demonstrated there, by various Experiments on the largest Scale of Dying, and to the entire Satisfaction of the most competent Judges, the Utility, Beauty, and Fixity of sundry Colours, namely, Blacks, Drabs, and Yellows, dyed from such indigenous Plants as may at all Times be found in the greatest Abundance in this Kingdom, and accordingly he has the Satisfaction of annexing to his Petition the Certificates, or Testimonials, of the Merchants, Manufacturers, and Dyers of the Town and Neighbourhood of Rochdale, in Lancashire, of the Clothiers Association at Saddle-worth, in the West Riding of Yorkshire, of the Merchants, Manufacturers, and Dyers, of the Towns and Neighbourhood of Halifax and Huddersfield, together with those of the Merchants and Manufacturers of Leeds, and also the Testimonial of the most eminent Cloth Factors in London, setting forth, that Woollen Goods, dyed according to the Petitioner's Mode, are 7 now

The Sixth Resolution of the Committee being read a Second Time;

Resolved, That, upon the Report of the List of the "Names of such absent Members, the Members, for whose Non-attendance, on the Appointment of any such Select Committee, a sufficient Excuse shall not be made, and allowed by the House, shall be forthwith ordered to be taken into the Custody of the Serjeant at Arms attending this House, and shall not be discharged out of Custody without the special Order of the House.

The Seventh Resolution of the Committee being read a Second Time;

Resolved, That this House will require, that strict Proof shall be given of the Facts and Circumstances which shall be alledged as a Cause of, or as an Excuse for, the Non-attendance of any Member, on the Appointment of any such Select Committee, as is above described.

A Petition of the several Persons whose Names are thereunto subscribed, being Owners of Houses and Ground situate in a certain Place called Holland's leagure, and in that Part of the Upper Ground Street which ‘lies on the East Side of Saint George's, or the High Road leading from Blackfriar's Bridge to the Obelisk, in Saint George's ,. in the Parish of

Christchurch, in the County of Surrey, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That by far the greater Part of the Houses and Buildings, situate in the said Part of the said Upper Ground Street, are in a ruinous State, and fit only to be pulled down, and the present Passage through the same is incommodious and dangerous; and that it would be of great public Utility if a new and commodious Street was formed from Saint George's Road, aforesaid, through the said Place called Holland's Leagure, into and across Vol. 48.

a certain other Place called The -Green Walk, and from thence into Gravel Lane, in the said Parish of Christchurch, and the same properly paved, cleansed, lighted, watched, and regulated, and that, when such New Street is made, the Passage through the said Part of the said Upper Ground Street will become useless; and that, as the said Part of the said Upper Ground Street lies on or near the Bank of the River Thames, it will tend greatly to the Advantage of the several Persons who are Owners of Houses, Wharfs, and Estates there, and would be of no Inconvenience to the Public, if that Part of the said Upper Ground Street was shut up, and the Passage through the same discontinued, and the Ground thereof laid into the said Wharfs and*

Estates, as soon as the said New Street shall have been laid out and completed: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for effecting the several Purposes aforesaid, in such Manner and under such Regulations, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Sir John Sinclair, Lord William Russell, 8cc.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

A Petition of the Gentlemen and Farmers, being Petition from Owners and Occupiers of Land in the Counties of Staffordshire Stafford and Salop, the Grain of which is generally sold respecting at Wolverhampton and its surrounding Manufactories, Canal Bills. was presented to the House, and read: Setting forth,

That the Scarcity of Workmen, and their consequent increased Wages during the last Harvest, was beyond all example, and attended with very considerable Loss to the Farmer, and to the Public, and to many of the Petitioners in particular, and if not obviated by some effectual Means may lead to Consequences of a very serious Nature; and that the Petitioners conceive the Scarcity of Workmen to have been materially owing to the Number of Canals making in various Parts of tire Kingdom, and that the Inconvenience arising from that Cause is likely to be very much increased by the additional Canals since projected: And therefore praying the House to take into Consideration the Propriety of inserting a Clause in the Bills for such Canals as are now pending, or may hereafter be brought before the House, to suspend the Workmen being employed therein during Two Harvest Months in every Year until such Canals be completed, or that the House Mould apply such other Remedy to the Evil complained of by the Petitioners as to the1 House may seem most fit.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

were appointed to try and determine the Merits of the j^^Ei^iou Petition of John Seale, Esquire, complaining of an determined, undue Election and Return for the Borough of Clifton Dartmouth Hardness, in the County of Devon, informed the House,

That it appeared to the said Select Committee,

That the Merits of the Petition did, in Part, depend upon the Right of Election; and that, thereupon, the said Committee required the Counsel for the several Parties to deliver to the Clerk of the said Committee Statements, in Writing, of the Right of Election for which they respectively contended.

That, in consequence thereof, the Counsel for the said Petitioner, John Seale, Esquire, delivered in a Statement, as follows:

"The Counsel for the Petitioner state, That the " Right of Election for the Borough of Clifton Dartmouth Hardness, in the County of Devon, is in the " Inhabitants of the said Borough, of which Borough " the Township or District, called Southiown, forms a " Part."

That the Counsel for the Sitting Members, the Right honourable John Charles Villiers, and Edmund Bastard, Esquire, delivered in a Statement, as follows:

" The Counsel for the Sitting Members state, That " the Right of Election for the Borough of " Dartmouth Hardness, in the County of Devon, is in the Freemen of the said Borough."

That, upon the Statement delivered in by the Counsel for the said Petitioner, the said Select Committee have determined,

That the Right of Election, as set forth in the said Statement, is not the Right of Election for the said Borough of Clifton Dartmouth Hardness.

That, upon the Statement delivered in by the Counsel for the Sitting Members, the said Select Committee have determined,

Mr. Pole Catea), from the Select Committee, who Pontefract were appointed to try and determine the Merits of the of Petition.of John Walsh, Esquire, who claims to be an termined. *" Elector of Representatives to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Pontefract, in the County of York.; and also, the Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed', who cl&im to be Electors of Representatives to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Pontefract, in the County of York; and also, thte Petition of John Smyth, and William Esquires,

respecting the Right of Election for the said Borough, informed the House.

That the Counsel for the Petition of John Walsh,

Esquire; and also the Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, who claim to be Electors of Representatives to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Pontefract, in the County of York, delivered in a Statement of the Right of Election for the said Borough, as follows:

" The Counsel for the opposing Petitions state,

" That the Right of Election of Members to serve in " Parliament for the Borough of Pontefract, in the " County of York, is in Persons having, within the said " Borough, a Freehold of Burgage Tenure paying a " Burgage Rent."

And that thereupon-the Counsel for the Petition of John Smyth and William Sotheron, Esquires, also delivered in a Statement of the Right of Election for the said Borough, as follows:

" The Counsel for the Petitioners in Support of the " Right of Election, as determined by the last Committee, state the Right of Election for the Borough " of Pontefract, to be in the Inhabitants Householders " Resiants."

That, upon the Statement delivered in by the Counsel for the Petition of John Walsh, Esquire; and also, for the Petition of the several Persons whose Names are thereunto subscribed, who claim to be Electors of Representatives to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Pontefract, in the County of York, the said Select Committee have determined.

That the Right of Election, as set forth in the said Statement, is not the Right of Election for the Borough of Pontefract, in the County of York.

That, upon the Statement delivered in by the Counsel for the Petition of John Smyth and William Sotheron, Esquires, the said Select Committee have determined,

That the Right of Election of Members to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Pontefract, in the County of York, is in the Inhabitants Householders Resiants.

And the said Determinations were ordered to be entered in the Journals of this House.

The other Orders of the Day being read;

Mr. Burke, one of the Members appointed by this Special Pro-House for managing the Trial of the Impeachment now ceedipge re-depending against Warren Hastings, Esquire, informed w e the House, That, the Lords having met this Day (before Hastin&s.* His Majesty came to the House of Peers) in the Chamber of Parliament, precisely at Twelve of the Clock, which is much earlier than their Lordships have usually assembled for the Purpose of going into Westminster Hall, their Lordships, without having given any Intimation to this House of their Intention to make this Alteration in the Time of their Proceeding, went at about Half an Hour after Twelve of the Clock, into Westminster Hall, before a sufficient Number of Members of this House were assembled for the Purpose of enabling Mr. Speaker to take the Chair — That, under these Circumstances, he (Mr. Burke) and such of the other Managers as were present in this House, thought it their Duty to appear in the Place appointed for the Managers in Westminster Hall, to be ready to go on with the Trial, without waiting for the usual Proceedings of this House on the Days appointed for the Trial; and that the Managers did accordingly appear in Westminster Hall, and the Trial proceeded.

And Mr. Burke desired to submit his Conduct, and that of the other Managers, upon this Occasion, to the Judgment of the House.;

Resolved, Nemine Contradicente, That under the Cir- Managers cumstances before mentioned, this House doth highly Conduct ap-approye of the Conduct of the Right honourable Edmund Proved* Burke, and the other Managers, in having taken such Steps as have enabled the Commons to proceed in the Trial of the said Impeachment.

Your Committee have therefore limited themselves to the Consideration of Two Points, which they have conceived may tend to expedite the Trial of this Impeachment:

First, the procuring a certain Attendance in this House at the Hour at which it is to meet on the Days of the Trial.

Secondly, The Means of Obtaining a greater Number of Days for the Trial, than has hitherto been granted in any One Session of Parliament.

Your Committee do not find that, during the whole Period of the Trial, the House of Lords have often had Occasion to wait for this House previous to their going into Westminster Hall; but they are obliged to admit,' that there has been in some Degree a Remissness in the Attendance in this House, which has sometimes prevented the Speaker from taking the Chair at the Hour when the Members ought to have attended.

Your Committee have not been able to suggest any Measure which could in itself compel a more exact Attendance in this House on the Days of the Trial,' but

Bill to re- A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to «>ns in mak- restra'n the employing of Labourers in making Na-ing Canals, vigable Canals, during the Time of the Corn Harvest;

An Amendment was proposed to be made to the Question, by leaving out the Word Labourers," and inserting the Words " any Persons'' instead thereof.

And the Question being put, That the Word " Labourers," stand Part of the Question;

It passed in the Negative.

And the Question being put, That the Words, " any " Persons" be inserted instead thereof;

It was resolved in the Affirmative.

Then the main Question, so amended, being put; Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to restrain the employing of any Persons in making Navigable Canals, during the Time of the Corn Harvest: And that Sir Charles Morgan, Sir George Howard, Mr. Powys, and Mr. Browne, do prepare, and

bring in, the same.

A Petition of the Owners and Occupiers of Lands Petition front within the respective Counties of and Derby, Staffordshire

assembled at a Meeting held at the White Hart Inn ^j*by

in Uttoxeter, in the County of Stafford, the 20th Rm«

Day of February i 793, pursuant to Public Advertisement, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners have, for several Harvests past, experienced a great Scarcity of Labourers, which they conceive, in some Measure, to be owing to the Numbers employed in cutting of Canals; and that the Petitioners observe, that many Applications have been, and now are, making to the House for Leave to bring in several Bills for the Purpose of making Canals in different Parts of this Kingdom^ whereby the Petitioners are aware that the Injuries they have sustained are likely to be increased to ani alarming Degree, to the great Injury of the Petitioners, and to the Public in general: And therefore praying, That their Case may be taken into Consideration, and that such Relief may be given them, in the Time of Hay and Corn Harvests, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for punishing Mutiny and Desertion, and for the better Payment of the Army and their Quarters; without any Amendment: And also,

Mr. Colhoun reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of several Inhabitants of the Town of Bedford, and also of several of the Trustees for putting in Execution an Act, passed in the Fourth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for enlarging the Charitable Uses, extending the Objects, and regulating the Application of the Rents and Profits of the Estates given by Sir William Haipu Knight, and Dame Alice his Wife, for the Benefit of the Poor, and other Objects of Charity, of the Town of Bedford, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the same, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the said Act was read: And,

Vo l. 48i

Mr. John Heaven being examined, said, That he has

known the Bedford Charity upwards of Forty Years, and has been Receiver of the Estates upwards of She Years; that the Charity is managed, and the Rents applied, under the Directions of the Act of the Fourth of His present Majesty; that the present Revenue of the Charity is 2,917/. 17 s.That at Midsummer next, about Seventy Leased now affecting the Charity Estate will expire; and at Lady Day 1794, Twelve or Thirteen other Leases will expire.

That by the Direction of the Trustees in November last, he caused the Estates to be advertised to be let upon repairing Leases, to commence at Midsummer next, and employed a Surveyor to survey the Premisses, and specify the Repairs necessary to be done to each House, and to estimate the probable Expence of the same, which was done, and entered in a Book, and deposited at his Office for Inspection; that he then advertised the same for Four Weeks, and Proposals were accordingly sent in; that the Houses were to be let separately, and no Fines to be taken, and that from the Proposals delivered; the probable Increase of the Revenue will be between Eight and Nine hundred Pounds per Annum.

That the present Act is insufficient for the well governing, regulating, and applying of the said Charity, and that it will be proper and expedient to extend and enlarge the Uses and Purposes to which the Income of the said Estate is, by the said Act, directed to be applied; but to enable the Trustees to do this a new Act is necessary; and that amongst the Regulations which are essential, the following present themselves as very material:

Under the present Act, no Person can be elected a Trustee, unless he has served the Office of Overseer; this has been found to operate to the Disadvantage of the C.harity, by Persons being elected who were unfit in point of Property and Station; the Necessity and Utility therefore of a more reputable Description of Inhabitants seems to be obvious; and that he conceives, that before any Trustee enters upon the Office of Trustee, that he should take an Oath, honestly, faithfully, and duly to serve the same. Under the present Act, any Person who holds a Place of Office or Profit under the Charity, or whose Child is bound out Apprentice with the Charity Money, may be elected a Trustee; it is therefore necessary that some Regulation should be made in this Particular, since no one can deny that the Dispensers of the Charity should not be the Participants of it: As the Act now stands, sufficient Notice is not given of the Election of a Trustee in Case of a Vacancy; besides the Notices given in Church after Divine Service, Notice should be alsd stuck on every Church Door in Bedford, and it should be pfoclaimea throughout the Town Two Days before every such Election.

That it will be an Incitement to Attention and Diligence in the Masters of the Charity Schools, who are appointed "by New College, Oxford, if they were to be allowed an Annual Sum for each Boy, exclusive of their Salaries: And it would be a very useful and praise-worthy Application of the Charity, if the Trustees granted Exhibitions for Scholars going to the University; and if Visitors were Annually appointed by New College, to examine the Boys, and Conduct of the Masters, neither of which Articles are provided for by the present Act. That the allowing Maid Servants to be Partakers of the Marriage Portions has been found productive of much Hurt to the Charity, by bringing into Bedford a great Number of Poof Girls from the adjacent Towns and Villages, to offer themselves as Servants at low Wages, ill order to gairi Settlements in the Town of Bedford, with a View of obtaining a Marriage Portion, which has experimentally tended to the Disadvantage of the Charity, and of the several Parishes in Bedford, and has very considerably

increased

Sevenoakes, Tunbridge . Wells, &c. Roads Petition reported,

4° Mctrti

A. 1793,

increased the Poors Rates there. The Poor Girls of the Town are by these Means also prevented from

fitting Places: — The Savings gained by abolishing larriage Portions might be applied to more useful Purposes.

The Hospital for the Support and Maintenance of the Poor Children, until fit to be bound out Apprentice, is admitted to be One of the most humane and useful Objects of the Charity, but the Sum allotted to this Object is very inadequate to the Purpose, and an additional Sum is proper to be applied, to this Institution.

That, by the present Act, a Trustee is not restricted from having any Contract for Building; such a Restriction is material, and will much tend to the Advantage of the Charity.

Petition against the Bill to extend the Birmingham and Birmingham and Fazely Canal Navigations.

A Petition of the Ironmongers, Factors, Manufacturers, Tradesmen, and other Inhabitants of the Borough and Foreign of Walsall, in the County of Stafford, and the Neighbourhood thereof, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the greater Part of the Petitioners are settled in the said Borough and Foreign of Walsall, and its Neighbourhood, and get their Living by manufacturing Iron, Steel, Copper, Brass, and other Metals, into Buckles, Chapes, Bridle Bits, Stirrups, Coach Furniture, Nails, and other heavy Articles, the Demand for which hath been increasing for many Years past, and the same are now arrived at such a Degree of Perfection and Extent, as to become an Object of great Concern to the Commerce and Wealth of this Kingdom; and that the Petitioners are informed, an Application is making to the House, by the Company of Proprietors of the Birmingham and Birmingham and Faxeley Canal Navigations, for Leave to bring in a Bill for making an Extension of One of the Branches or Collateral Cuts of the Birmingham and Birmingham and Faxeley Canal Navigations, from its present Termination near Broadwater, in the Parish of in the County of Stafford, through the Liberty or Township of Bilston, in the Parish of Wolverhampton, to the several Parishes of Wednesbury and Darlasttm, to or near a Place called Bilston Bridge, in the Liberty or Township of Bilston, in the said Parish of Wolverhampton, with a Collateral Branch or Cut from such Extension, to or near a Bridge on the Turnpike Road leading from Willenhall to Walsall, called County Bridge', and, the Petitioners beg Leave to observe, that the said Company of Proprietors have, by virtue of various Acts of Parliament, already made a Number of Extensions and Collateral Branches, from the said Birmingham and Birmingham and Faxeley Canal, to and through the Coal Mines in the Neighbourhood of Bilston, Wednesbury, Bradley, Willingsuorth, Tipton, and Darlaston, in the said County of Stafford, by which they are now enabled to take and convey the same to the Birmingham and other Markets, without the projected Extension to Bilston Bridge and County Bridge, in their said Petition named, and to have them at a cheaper Rate than the Petitioners in the Neighbourhood of the said Mines; and representing to the House, that, in consequence of the advanced Price of Coal, and the great Increase of the Petitioners said Manufactories, and having, at present, no Communication by Water to the said Coal Mines, and heavily experiencing the great Expence of Land Carriage, they, together with the City of the principal

Mine Owners, and other Persons, intend to apply to the House, in the next Session of Parliament, for an Act to make and maintain a Navigable Canal to communicate with the said Coal Mines, which the Petitioner will be prevented from doing, if the said Extension is permitted to be made, by reason it will encircle the said Mines in such a Manner, that neither the Petitioners, nor any part of the Country on the North-East Side of the said proposed Extensions, can get at, or have a Canal Communication, to the said Mines, without intersecting or crossing the said proposed Branches or Extensions, whereby they will be deprived of their equal Right of ]participating in so necessary and essential an Article in their said Manufactories as Coal by W ater Carriage, and, at the same Time, the Petitioners beg Leave to repeat, that the Birmingham Canal Company, having already a Communication with the said Mines sufficient to convey the same to Birmingham, as aforesaid, the proposed Extensions, therefore, are most certainly a Scheme to encircle and circumscribe the said Mines, and thereby prevent the Petitioners from having a Canal Communication therewith, which will be of essential Advantage to the populous manufacturing Town and Neighbourhood of Walsall, and to the Lime Mines there, as also to the City of Litchfield, and the intermediate Places, by affording them a regular Supply of Coals at a more reasonable Price than they are now supplied, and also rendering the Carriage of their heavy manufactured Goods and Merchandize less expensive, and will be of great Public Utility; and that the said intended Extensions terminate at uninhabited Places between Walsall and the said Coal Mines, and the said County Bridge is not more than Two Miles from Walsall, therefore, it evidently appears from such Terminations, that the same can answer no other Purpose than as hereinbefore stated by the Petitioners, who rely on the House for Protection against die unbounded Spirit of Monopoly and Aggrandizement attempted by the said proposed Extensions of the said Birmingham and Birmingham and Faxeley Canal, and that the said Coal Mines, the fundamental Support of their Manufactures, may be preserved and secured against such partial interested Views: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill, and that the same may not pass into a Law.

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Ord and Mr.

Walker:

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for reviving, continuing, and amending, certains Acts of the Fourteenth and Thirtieth Years of King George the Second, so far as relates to repairing the Road from the North End of Wakefield Bridge to Halifax, in the West Riding of the County of York', without any Amendment: And also,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to provide for the Families of Persons chosen by Lot to serve in the Militia of this Kingdom, and of Substitutes serving the rein, and to explain and amend an Act of Parliament, passed in the Twenty-sixth Year of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for amending, and reducing into One Act of Parliament, the " Laws relating to the Militia in that Part of Great Britain called England," without any Amendment:

And also,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from, or nearly from, a Place called The Saltisford, in the Parish of Saint Mary, in the Borough of Warwick, unto, or near to, the Parish of Birmingham, in the County of Warwick, and to terminate at, or near to, a certain Navigable Canal, in, or near to, the Town of Birmingham, called The Digbeth Branch of the Birmingham and Birmingham and Fazeley Canal Navigations', with some Amendments'; to which Amendments the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

Mr. Alderman Curtis accordingly reported from the said Committee, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed to be reported to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee* That so much of an Act, passed in the Twenty-second Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, as is expressed to be for the Purpose of promoting the Brewing of good Table Beer, has been proved, from the great Advance in Price on the Articles of Malt and Hops, as well as on the other constituent Parts of the Capital of a Common Brewer, to be inadequate to the intended Purpose.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient, in order to answer the Purpose of the said Act, that the Common Brewer should be permitted to brew for Sale Tabic Beer, at a higher Vol. 48.

33 Geo. III. 4° Martii. 331

Resolution on considering Report respecting limiting, &c. of Tolls imposed by Navigation Bills reported.

Ordered, That the said Account and Estimates do lie upon the Table to be perused by the Members of the House.

Sir George Howard',according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of the Report which was made from the Committee, who were appointed to consider of a Mode of limiting, regulating, and applying, the Produce of the Tolls to be imposed by all Bills now depending, or which shall hereafter be introduced into this House, for making Navigable Canals, in such Manner as may best reconcile the Interests of the Undertakers with the public Benefit, the Resolution which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth;

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it will be proper and expedient to regulate, in future, the Transfer of Shares in all Undertakings for making Navigable Canals, and that the Transfer of such Subscriptions to such intended Canals should be prohibited for a certain. Time after such Subscriptions shall have been made.

The said Resolution being read a Second Time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That a Bill be brought in upon the said Resolution: And that Sir George Howard, the Master of the Rolls, Mr. Powys, and Sir John Call, do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Committee The House, according to Order, resolved itself into on American a Committee of the whole House, upon the Bill to Trade Bill. continue the Laws now in Force for regulating the Trade between the Subjects of His Majesty's Dominions and the Inhabitants of the Territories belonging to the United States of America, so far as the same relate to the Trade and Commerce carried on between this Kingdom and the Inhabitants of the Countries belonging to the said United States.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Henry Hobart took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Henry Hobart reported from the Committee, That they had gone through the Bill, and made several Amendments thereunto; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received Tomorrow Morning.

Address for Copies of Representations on the Newfoundland Trade and Fishery, &c.

Resolved, That an humble Address be presented to His Majesty, that He will be graciously pleased to give Directions that there be laid before this House, Copies or Extracts of Three Representations of the Lords Commissioners for Trade and Plantations to His Majesty upon the Newfoundland Trade and Fishery, dated the 19th Day of December 1718, the 29th Day of April 1765, and the 27th Day of March 1766; and also, of a Report of the Lords of the Committee of Privy Council for Trade and Foreign Plantations on the Newfoundland Fishery, &. c. dated the 17 th Day of March 1786; and also, of a Representation on the Subject of establishing a Court of Civil Judicature in Newfoundland, dated the 10th Day of May 1790.

Ordered, That the said Address be presented to His Majesty, by such Members of this House as are of His Majesty's most Honourable Privy Council.

Petition A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Trades-

agaiost men, and other Inhabitants of the Town and County Caul BUlT of the Town of Nottingham, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are informed that Application is intended to be made to Parliament, in this present Session, for a Bill to make a Navigable Canal from the Town of Derby into and through the Trent and Mersey Canal to the River Trent near to Swarkstone, in the County of Derby, and another Navigable Canal from the said Town of Derby to the Erewash Canal, which falls into the said River Trent about Two Miles below Shardlow, in the said County, and another Navigable Canal from Derby aforesaid to, or near to, a Place called Denby, in the said County; and that the Petitioners are of Opinion that a Canal from the said Town of Derby to the Trent and Mersey Canal at Shardlow, in Length about Six Miles only, and from or near Shardlow to the said Town of Nottingham, for which a Petition is intended to be presented to Parliament, will be of more general Utility to the said Town of Nottingham, and to the Public, and will be executed at much less Expence than the Three Canals first above-mentioned: And therefore prating, That they may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill for the said Three Canals, and that the same may not pass.

A Petition of the Mayor and Burgesses of the Town and County of the Town of Nottingham, in Common Hall assembled, was also presented to the House, and read; Containing the same Allegations and Prayer as the last preceding Petition.

A Petition of the Company of Proprietors of the Navigation from the Trent to the Mersey, was likewise presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, by virtue of various Acts, passed in the present Reign, the Petitioners have, at great Expence and Hazard, completed a Navigable Canal from the River Trent, at or near Shardlow, in the County of Derby, to the River Mersey, at Runcorn, in the County of Chester, which has been productive of great Public

Vo l. 48.

Advantage; and that the Petitioners observe, by the Votes, that Application is making to the House for a Bill to make a Canal for the Passage of Barges, and other Vessels, from the River Trent, at or near a certain Place, called Swarkstone Bridge, to the Town of Derby, into, across, and through the Navigation of the Petitioners, and the Banks and lowing Paths thereof, and to make Locks out of the same down to the said River, which is near Twenty Feet lower than the said Navigation from the Trent to the Mersey, at Swarkstone aforesaid; and that such proposed Canal, if authorized to be made and cut into and through the said Navigation, and to draw off the Waters that support and maintain the same, will be an Infringement and Violation of the Rights of the Petitioners, and highly injurious to their Property, and will form a Precedent of the most alarming and dangerous Tendency to every Person engaged in the Works of Inland Navigation; and that the Injuries, to be apprehended by the Petitioners from the said proposed Canal, are the more aggravated by the Circumstance of the said Canal not forming the most eligible Line of Communication with the said Town of Derby, a Bill being now depending for making a Canal from the Navigation of the Petitioners at Shardlow to the Town of Derby, with an Extension to or near the Town of Nottingham, which will open a safe, certain, and easy Communication between the said Towns, and many other large Trading Towns and Places, and be of much more general Utility, not only to the said Town of Derby, but to the Public, than the said Canal from Swarkstone aforesaid, without being injurious to the Petitioners: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill for making a Canal from Swarkstone Bridge to Derby, and that the Bame may not pass into a Law.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table, until the Bill for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the River Trent, at, or near, a certain Place called Swarkstone Bridge, to and through the Liberty of the Borough of Derby, to Little,

Sir George Hotvard reported from the Committee, Stamford to whom the Petition of the several Persons, whose p*^"*'*' Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of them- porle(j. selves and others, Inhabitants within the Borough of Stamford, and the Precincts thereof, in the County of Lincoln, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, and Bills of Inclosure, had been complied with, except that the Notice, required by the Standing Orders of the House to be given at the Michaelmas Quarter Sessions, had not been given till the Christmas Quarter Sessions, and that, as no Toll was intended to be taken, nor the Public any Way burthened, it was apprehended that the Standing Orders would not attach; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the same, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr.

Hugh Jackson and Mr . George Jackson being examined, said, That the Streets, Lanes, Passages, and Causeways, within the said Borough and Precincts, are not properly paved, cleansed, lighted, or watched, and some of them are very narrow, and, on Account of many Obstructions, Nuisances, and Annoyances, are rendered unsafe, dangerous, and incommodious, to all Persons passing along the same — That it would conduce to the Safety and Convenience of all Persons residing within, or resorting to, the said Borough, if the said Streets, Lanes, Passages, and Causeways, were properly paved, cleansed, lighted, watched, and regulated, and if such of them as are too narrow were widened, and all Encroachments, Nuisances, Annoyances, and Obstructions therein, were removed, and prevented for the future. — That in the said Borough and Precincts there is a certain Common, called Tenter Meadoto, and also several Waste Grounds, or Waste Places, which are, in their present State, of very little Benefit to the Persons interested therein; but if the same, or so much as shall be found requisite, were inclosed, all Right of Common abolished, and the said Meadow and Waste Grounds sold, or let on Building or other Leases, and the Money arising therefrom applied towards the Expences of paving, lighting, cleansing, watching, and improving the said Borough and Precincts, it would be very advantageous to the Inhabitants thereof, and all Persons interested in the said Lands and Grounds.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill, for paving, cleansing, lighting, watching, and regulating the several Streets, Lanes, Passages, and Causeways, within the Borough of Stanford, and Precincts thereof, in the County of Lincoln, for removing and preventing Nuisances, Annoyances, and Encroachments therein, and for widening some of the Streets and Lanes within the said Borough and Precincts:

And that Sir George Howard, the Earl of Carysfort, and Mr. Heathcote, do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Petition A Petition of the Commissioners, whose Names are

Shipton and hereunto subscribed, appointed by the several Acts of

Isleworth Parliament made for improving and completing the

Canal Bill. Navigation of the Rivers Thames and Isis, from the Jurisdiction of the City of London near Staines, in the County of Middlesex, to the Town of Cricklade, in the County of Wilts, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners, by the Authority, and in pursuance of the Directions, of the said several Acts, have borrowed, on the Security of the Tolls of the said Navigation, a considerable Sum of Money, and therewith have amended the Navigation of the said Rivers from Staines to Lechlade, being an Extent of about One hundred Miles, throughout which, in consequence of the said Amendments, the Carriage of Goods on the said Navigation is rendered more cheap, safe, certain, and expeditious; that the Petitioners have no private Interests in the said Public Undertaking, they receive no Emolument whatever for acting as Commissioners, and cannot act where they are interested, the Creditors only receive legal Interest for the Money they have lent on the Credit of the Tolls, and all Surplusses (after paying necessary Expences) are to be applied for Public Benefit, by reducing the Debt or lessening the Tolls; and that the Petitioners observe, by the Votes of the House, that a Bill hath been brought in for Powers to make and maintain a Navigable Canal, to be called The London and Western Canal, out of the Oxford Canal Navigation, within the Parish of Shipton, in the County of Oxford, and, after passing through Parts of the County of Bucks near and Amer-

sham, to join or communicate with the River Thames at or near Isleworth, in the County of Middlesex, the Line of which intended Canal, in many Parts of it, passes so near to the Navigation of the said Rivers, so improved by the Petitioners, that they conceive, if the said Bill should pass into a Law, and the said Canal be made, it will be, in the highest Degree, injurious to the Navigation of the Thames and Isis by intercepting, cutting off, or diverting, several Springs, or Streams of Water, which have usually flowed, and do now flow, into the said Rivers, and materially lessen the Depth of Water therein, especially in all dry Seasons, and thereby, and by other Means, obstructing, intercepting, and diverting, the ancient Trade and Intercourse w'hich hath long subsisted by the said Navigation to the great Convenience and Benefit of the Towns of Abingdon, Wallingford, Reading, Henky, Marlow, Maidenhead, Windsor, and other Places on the Banks of the Thames and Isis, and will also unavoidably lessen the Security for the Money which hath been lent at legal Interest, on the Faith of Parliament, for the Improvement of the Thames and Isis: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by themselves, or Counsel, against the said Bill being passed into a Law, or have such other Relief in the Premises as to the House shall . seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, until the Bill for making and maintaining a Vol. 48.

Navigable Canal, from and out of, the Oxford Canal Navigation, within the Parish of Shipton, in the County of Oxford, to join and communicate with the River Thames at or near Isleworth, in the County of Middlesex, be read a Second Time; and that the Petitioners be then heard, by themselves, or Counsel, against the said Bill, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That Counsel be admitted to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. John Collins being examined, said, That the Roads described in the Petition are very much out of Repair, and during several Months in the Year are dangerous to Horsemen, and from their Narrowness, in many Places, are nearly impassable for Carriages; and that the same cannot be effectually repaired, widened, secured against Floods, and kept in Repair, by the ordinary Course of Law.

And the Witness further said, That the Repair of the said Roads will be of great Public Utility, by opening a Communication between the Towns of Lincoln, Nottingham, and Derby, and the Town of Shrewsbury and North Wales; and also between the Towns of Stafford and Cannock, and the large Manufacturing Towns of Walsall and Birmingham.

Troops.

GEORGE R.

His Majesty having judged it expedient to employ in the Service of Great Britain a Body of His Llectoral Troops, for the Purpose of assisting His Allies the States General of the United Provinces, and of prosecuting in the most effectual Manner the ju6t and necessary War in which His Majesty is engaged, His Majesty has directed an Estimate to be laid before the House of Commons of the Charge attending the Employment of the said Troops; and His Majesty relies on the Zeal of His faithful Commons, that they will be ready to make the necessary Provision for maintaining the same.

Ordered, That His Majesty's said most Gracious Message be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to consider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty.

Petition for A Petition of the several Merchants and Owners of Provision in Vessels trading to Littleha in the Port of Littlehamp- in the County of Sussex, whose Names are thereunto ton Harbour subscribed, on Behalf of themselves and other Mer-®'11* chants and Owners of Vessels.

And the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That, by an Act made in the Sixth Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, for erecting Piers in, and for repairing and keeping in Repair, the Harbour of,

called Arundel Port, in the County of Sussex, certain Persons therein named, and their Successors, were appointed Commissioners for improving and preserving the said Harbour, to make a new Cut or Channel through the Sea Beach there, and to erect and make such Pier and Piers, Lock or Locks, and to do such other Works as should be thought necessary and convenient for the Purposes aforesaid; and Powers were thereby given to the said Commissioners to collect the several Rates and Duties, thereby made payable for sundry Kinds of Merchandize and Tonnage of Vessels, and to assign the same as a Security for Money to be borrowed, in pursuance and for the Purposes of the said Act; and, it was thereby further enacted, that when the said Commissioners were, by the said Duties, fully reimbursed the Principal Monies by them borrowed and laid out for the Purposes aforesaid, together with all Interest and Charges attending the same, One Half Part of the said Duties should cease, and the other Half thereof should continue, and be collected and paid, for keeping the said Pier or Piers, Lock or Locks, and other Works, in good and sufficient Repair, and for maintaining, keeping, and preserving, the said Harbour and River navigable; and that a large Sum of Money was subscribed and borrowed for the Purposes in the said Act mentioned, and Piers and Locks were erected, and a new Cut or Channel was made, in pursuance of the Directions therein contained, and all the Monies, subscribed for and borrowed by virtue of the said Act, together with Interest for the same, and all Claims whatever on the said Commissioners, in respect of the said Harbour, Piers, and Works, having been paid and satisfied, One Moiety, or Half Part, of all the Duties respectively granted by the said Act, hath accordingly ceased and determined; and that a Bill is now depending in the House, to explain and amend an Act, made in the Sixth Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, intituled, "An Act for erecting Piers in, and for repairing and keeping in Repair, the Harbour of Littlehampton, called " Arundel Pert, in the County of and for em-

powering the Commissioners acting under the said Act, to improve the Navigation of the River Arun, from the said Harbour, to the Town of Arundel, in the said County, which Bill is to enable the Commissioners therein named to apply the Money already raised, and in the Treasurer's Hands, and also the Money hereafter to be paid by virtue of the said Act of the Sixth Year of his late Majesty's Reign, for the Purpose of making a Haling or Towing Track from Littlehampton to Arundel, from which Towing Track no Benefit can arise to the Petitioners, although they contribute so largely to the Pier Dues, their vessels being too large to be navigated farther than Littlehampton; and that the Piers, &c. at Littlehampton, for the Repair of which the said Rates or Pier Does are paid and payable, under or by virtue of the Sixth of George the Second, are, at this Time, much out of Re-

pair, and (as the Petitioners are advised by experienced Workmen) not only the Money now in Hand, but the whole Tolls to be collected for Seven Years from this Time, will be wanted (within that Period) to be laid out in maintaining and repairing the said Piers, &c. so that if the Money raised by virtue of the said Act is applied in making a Haling or Towing Track, the Petitioners have reason to believe that it will be necessary to apply for a new Act to raise Money to repair and maintain the Piers, &c. although there is at present a Fund, which, together with the Dues to be hereafter collected, will be sufficient to answer all the Purposes intended by tl»e said Act of the Sixth of George the Second: And therefore praying, That their Case may be taken into Consideration, and that the said Bill now before the House may be so far altered, that the Tolls, Rates, or Dues, for repairing the Piers, &c. at Littlehampton, may not be applied in making a Haling or Towing Track to ,or

for any other Purposes than as by the said Act is directed.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the said Bill i6 committed.

Ordered, That all who come to the said Committee have Voices.

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

Three Shillings per Chalder or Ton on Coals, and Three Shillings per Chalder on Culm, for the building of Fifty Churches in and near the Cities of London and Westminster, and for certain other local Purposes specified in the aforesaid Acts; and that, in consequence of the ImpoatB of Five perCent. granted in the Years 1779 and 1782 by the Acts of the Nineteenth of George the Third, Cap. 25, and the Twenty-second of George the Third, Cap. 66, together with Additions by the Consolidation Act, of the Twenty-seventh of George the Third, Cap. 13, to raise the Fractions to Integers, the aforesaid local Duties have been augmented to Three Shillings and Four Pence per Chalder or Ton on Coals, and Three Shillings and Three Pence per Chalder on Culm, and it appears, by Computations now made, that, prior to the Year 1731, the Produce of the local Duties had made good a full Compensation to Government for the Expence of the local Benefits conferred:

Ordered \That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Henry Hobart, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of the several Accounts, Papers, and Reports, which have been presented to this House, in this Session of Parliament, from the Directors of the East India Company, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth;

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That, on an Average of Three Years, 1787 to 1789-90 inclusive, the Revenues of the several Presidencies of Bengal, Madras, and Bombay, have amounted to Six Millions Eight hundred and Ninety-seven thousand Seven hundred and Thirty Pounds per Annum, and the Charges incurred in the Civil and Military Establishments, as far as can be ascertained, to Five Millions Two hundred and Thirty-three thousand Seven hundred and Seventeen Pounds per , valuing

the Current Rupee at Two Shillings, the Star Pagoda at Eight Shillings and the Rupee at Two

Shillings and Three Pence.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That, allowing Fifty thousand Pounds per Annum for the Expences of Bencoolen and Penang, the Net Revenues of the British Possessions in India on the foregoing Average, have amounted to One Million Six hundred and Fourteen thousand and Thirteen Pounds per Annum.

Resolved', That it appears to this Committee, That the Revenues arising from the Countries ceded to the Company by Tippoo Sultaun at the Termination of the late War, stated in the Treaty at Thirteen Lacks, Sixteen thousand Seven hundred and Sixty-five Pagodas, and which Countries are estimated, by the Court of Directors, to produce Three hundred and Ninety thousand Pounds per Annum, are npt included in the foregoing Average Amount of Revenues.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the future Revenues of the British Possessions in India are estimated, by the Court of Directors, to amount to Six Millions Nine hundred and Sixty-three thousand Six hundred and Twenty-five Pounds per Annum, and the Civil and Military Charges (including One hundred and Four thousand Four hundred and Fifty Pounds for Commercial Charges) to Five Millions Three hundred and Forty-two thousand Five hundred and seventy-five Pounds per Annum.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the Net Revenues of the British Provinces in India, after defraying the Civil, Military, and Commercial Charges, are estimated, by the Court of Directors, at One Million Six hunched and Twenty-one thousand1 and Fifty Pounds.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the Debts owing by the East India Company at the several Settlements in India amounted, on the 31st Day of January 1792, as dear as can Be ascertained, to the Sum of Nine Crore, Eight Lacks, Forty-five thousand1 Five hundred and Eight Current Rupees.

Resoltoed, That it appears to1 this Committee, That the Amount of the Debt, bearing Interest, on the 31st Day of January 1792, was Six Crore; Ninety-three1 Lacks, Thirty-nine thousand Four hundred and' Thirty-two Current Rupees, and1 that the1 Amount of that Interest was Fifty-nine Lacks, Twenty-two thousand and Ninety Current Rupees; but that, from later Advices, the Amount of DfeBt bearing Interest isi stated by the Court of Directors at Six Millions Six

Vo 1.. 48.

hundred and Sixty-nine thousand and Eighty-two Pounds, and the Amount of that Interest at Fire hundred and Sixty-one thousand Nine hundred and Twenty three Pounds.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That, after deducting the Interest payable on the Debts in India, from the Excess of the Revenues above the Civil, Military, and Commercial Charges, the Net Surplus is estimated at One Million and Fifty-niofe thousand One hundred and Twenty-sevten Pounds per Annum.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That, on the Average of the Three last Years, from the 1st Day of March 1790 to 1793, the Prime Cost of Goods sold by the East India Company has amounted to Two Millions Fivo hundred and Fifty thousand Seven hundred and Twenty-eight Pounds per that

the Customs payable on those Goods has amounted tb Six hundred and Twelve thousand Two hundred and Thirty-one Pounds per Annum, the Charges df Freight and Demorage to Seven hundred and Seventeen thousand Four hundred and Fifty-three Pounds, and the Charges of Merchandize to Three hundred and Six thousand One hundred and Eighty-five Pounds per Annum, making the Total of Prime*Cost and Charges Four Millions One hundred and Eighty-six thousand Five hundred and Ninety-seven Pounds per Annum.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the Goods sold by the Company in the last Three Years, on an Average, have amounted to Five Millions One hundred and Three thousand and Ninety-four Pounds per Annum, which exceeds the Prime Cost and Charges by Nine hundred and Sixteen thousand Four hundred and Ninety-seven Pounds.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the Prime Cost, and several Charges of Customs, Freight, and Charges of Merchandize, of the Goods to be sold by the East India Company, are estimated, by the Court of Directors, to amount to Four Millions Two hundred and Forty-four thousand Six hundred and Ninety-eight Pounds per Anrium.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the Sales of Goods by the East India Company are estimated, by the Court of Directors to amount to Four Millions Nine hundred and Eighty-eight thousand Three hundred Pounds per Annum, which exceeds the Prime Cost and Charges by Seven hundred and Forty-three thousand Six hundred and Two Pounds.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That the Charges and Profit on Private Trade, on the Average of the last Three Years, have amounted to Eighty-three thousand Three hundred and Ninety-three Pounds per Annum, and are estimated, by the Court of Directors, to amount to Seventy thousand Pounds per Annum in future.

Resolved, That it appears to fthis Committee, Tha£ the Net Surplus on the Whole of the Revenues and Trade of the East India Company* after paying Eight per Cent. Dividend on the Capital Stock of Five MHr lions, is estimated, by the Court of irectors, to amount to One Million Two hundred and Thirty-nine thousand Two hundred and Forty-one Pounds per Annum.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, That, in the last Three Years, Two Millions Eight hundred and Twenty-one thousand One hundred and Eighty-three Pounds of the Principal and Interest of die Dfebt transferred from India to England, has been discharged1 by the East India Company.

Resolved, That it appears to this Committee, THaf die Debts owing by the Eetst India Company at Home, under the Head of Annuities, Bonds, BiHs of Exchange, Customs, and Debtis contracted in the ordinary Course of their Commereia!l, Transactions, are' calculated to amount, on the 1st Day of March 1793

East India Company's Petition.

A Petition of the United Company of Merchants of England trading to the East Indies, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners, having received such Notice as is required by Law to be given to them for determining their exclusive Trade on the 1st Day of March 1794, are desirous to renew the said Trade, and have prepared a Petition to the House for that Purpose, but the Time for receiving private Petitions being expired, the same cannot be presented without Leave; and that, on account of the Length and Variety of the various Accounts, and other Matters, necessary to be considered and prepared for the Business of the Renewal of the said exclusive Trade, the Petitioners were not able to present the said Petition within the Time limited for presenting private Petitions: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to the Petitioners now to present a Petition to the House, for Leave to bring a Bill into the House, for enlarging the Term of the Petitioners exclusive Trade, and for continuing the Government and Management of the Territorial Acquisitions and Revenues in the East Indies, in the Manner prescribed by the Laws now in Force, without Prejudice to the Rights of the Petitioners, or the Claim of the Public, as in a former Act is provided.

Ordered, That in Consideration of the particular Circumstances set forth in the said Petition, Leave bo

g'ven to present a Petition as desired by the said United ompany of Merchants of England trading to the East Indies.

Then a Petition of the United Company of Merchants of England, trading to the East Indies, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, by an Act made in the Twenty-first Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for establish-' ing an Agreement with the United Company of " Merchants of England, trading to the East Indies, " for the Payment of the Sum of Four hundred thousand Pounds, for the Use of the Public, in foil Discharge and Satisfaction of all Claims and Demands " of the Public, from the Time the Bond Debt of the tl said Company was reduced to One Million Five " hundred thousand Pounds, until the First Day of March One thousand Seven hundred and Eightyone, in respect of the Territorial Acquisitions and " Revenues lately obtained in the East Indies, and also " for securing to the Public, in respect thereof, for a " Term therein mentioned, a certain Part or Propor-u tion of the clear Revenues and Profits of the said " Company; and for granting to the said Company, " for a further Term, the sole and exclusive Trade to " and from the East Indies, and Limits therein menhoned; and for establishing certain Regulations for " the better Management of the Affairs of the said " Company, as well in India as in Europe, and for " Recruiting the Military Forces of the said Company," it was, amongst other Things, enacted, That the Petitioners ('subject to the Proviso of Determination thereinafter contained) should have, use, and enjoy, the whole, sole, and exclusive Trade and Traffic into and from the East Indies, and into and from all Places between the Cape of Good Hope, and Streights of Magellan, and that they should have, hold, and enjoy, and be entitled unto all Advantages, Privileges, Franchises, and Authorities whatsoever, which by any former Acts, or by any Charters, founded thereupon, were enacted, given, granted, or established, concerning the Petitioners, and the other Societies, or Com-Vox.. 48.

parties, therein mentioned, and not by that Act altered, or intended to be altered, according to the true Meaning of the said Acts and Charters, and the same were thereby ratified and confirmed, in which Act is contained a Proviso, that at any Time, upon Three Years Notice to be given by Parliament, after the 1st Day of March 1791, upon the Expiration of the said Three Years, and Re-payment to the Petitioners of the Debt of 4,200,000 due to them for the Public, and all Arrears of Annuity payable in respect thereof, in case the same should not have been before re-paid, then and from thenceforth, and not before or sooner, the said Right, Title, and Interest of the Petitioners, to the whole, sole, and exclusive Trade to the East and Parts aforesaid, should cease and determine; and, by the said Act, it was further enacted, That any Notice in Writing, signified by the Speaker of the House of Commons for the Time being, by Order of the said House, should be deemed and judged a due and proper Notice by Parliament, and it was further enacted, That all the Territorial Acquisitions and Revenues lately obtained in the East Indies, should remain in the Possession of the Petitioners for and during the Term of the exclusive Trade granted to them, and, by the said Act, an Appropriation was made, agreeable to the Petitioners Agreement, of the clear Profits arising from the said Territorial Acquisitions and Revenues, together with the Petitioners clear Revenues and Profits arising during the Continuance of the said whole, sole, and exclusive Trade and Traffic; and the said Act was subject to a further Proviso, that nothing therein contained should extend, or be construed to extend, to prejudice or affect the Rights or Claims of the Public, or the Petitioners, respecting the said Territorial Acquisitions and Revenues, as by the said Act may more at large appear; and that the Notice required by the said Act of Parliament hath been given by the Speaker of this House for determining the exclusive Trade of the Petitioners on the 1st Day of March 1794; and Representing to the House, that the System established by the said Act for the Government of the Territorial Acquisitions in the East Indies, for the Management of the Revenues, and for conducting the Affairs of the Petitioners, aided by the Regulations since introduced by the Wisdom of Parliament, hath been approved by Experience: And, as such Experience affords just Reason to believe, that a Continuance of such System will prove equally advantageous to the Public and to the Petitioners, therefore praying, That Leave may be

f'ven to bring in a Bill for enlarging the Term of the etitioners said exclusive Trade, and for continuing the Government and Management of the said Territorial Acquisitions and Revenues, in the Manner prescribed by the stud Acts of Parliament, without Prejudice to the Rights of the Petitioners, or the Claim of the Public, as in the former Act is provided.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Committee of the Company of Merchants trading to Africa, being offered, to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners have laid before the House, an Account of the Money granted for the Year 3791, examined and passed by the Cursitor Baron of the Exchequer, as required by an Act of the Twenty-third of George the Second, intituled, "An Act for " extending and improving the Trade to Africa," and that they have invested the Money, granted in 1792, for the Support and Maintenance of the Forts and Settlements on the said Coast; and that the Forts having been originally ill constructed, were delivered to the Petitioners in a very ruinous Condition by the Royal African Company, and, being composed of the very worst Materials, are falling so continually into Decay as to require a larger Expenditure in Repairs than can be afforded out of the Sums Annually granted by Parliament, and the War now broke out between Great Britain and France will cause a great additional Expence in Freight and Insurance on the future Investments of the said Committee: And that the Petitioners, being sensible of the great Regard shewn by the House for the Preservation, Improvement, and Extension of the Trade to Africa, and for the Defence and Maintenance of the British Forts and Settlements on that Coast, therefore pray the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and grant the Sum Annually voted for the Support and Maintenance of the said Forts, and for such other Purposes as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Wilberforce reported from the Committee, to Additional whom the Petition of the Company of Proprietors of Petition to the Canal Navigation from Leeds to Liverpool, was Li^poof referred; That the Committee had examined, and canalNavi-found that the said Petition is not within the Stand- gation Bill ing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bills, reported-it not being intended to raise any further or additional Rates, Tolls, or Duties; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the same, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table:

Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the Tenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for making and maintaining a Navigable Cut or Canal from " Leeds Bridge, in the County of York, to The North " Lady's Walk, in Liverpool, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, and from thence to the River " Mersey,'' was read: And,

Mr. John Hardy being examined, said, That there is no Power in the Act to prevent Water being taken from the Canal without Leave of the Company, and to enable them to make Waggon and Railways, where necessary; and that the Act is in other Respects defective.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the Committee, to whom the Bill to enable the Company of Proprietors of the Canal Navigation from Leeds to Liverpool to vary the Line of the said Canal Navigation, and to raise a further Sum of Money for the Purpose of completing the said Canal Navigation, and for other Purposes, is committed, That they have Power to make Provision in the said Bill for amending and enlarging the Powers of an Act, passed in the Tenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making, and maintaining a Navigable Cut or Canal from Leeds Bridge, in the County of York, to The North Lady's Walk, in Liverpool, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, and from thence to the River Mersey.

To prove- the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. William Jessop being examined, said, That it appears, by Surveys and Levels lately taken, that a Canal, navigable for Boats and other Vessels, may be made from the River Colder, in the Township of cum Heath, to or near the Township of Barnsley, and from thence to Bamby Bridge, and also One other Cut branching out of the said Canal, near and

ending at or near Haigh Brall in the County of York: — Then,

Mr. Elias Wright being examined, said, That the making of such Canal and Cut, together with proper Waggon, Railed, and other Roads and Ways to communicate therewith, will be attended with very great Benefit and Advantage to all Owners of Estates, Merchants, Manufacturers, Tradesmen, and Residents, near to the said intended Canal, and also to the City of York, the Towns of Malton, Selby, and Hull, and many other populous and considerable Towns and Places, where extensive Works and Manufactories of various Kinds, and great Traffick are carried on, in the County of York and other Counties, as the said Canal will pass through a Tract of Country in which are very large Quantities of Coal and Ironstone, and will afford a cheap, easy, and expeditious Conveyance for Corn, Lime, and other Goods, Wares, and Merchandizes, to and from the Places lying in or near to the Line thereof.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are Petition to thereuuto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves and' other Merchants, Tradesmen, and Inhabitants of the Chelmsford Town and Port of Maldon, in the County of Essex, Navigation, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth.

That the Petitioners are informed, that Application is making to Parliament for a Bill for making and maintaining a Navigation from the Town of Chelmsford to a Place called Colliers Reach, in the River Blackwater, below the said Town and Port of Maldon, by Means of widening, deepening, and improving the Rivers C'hel-mer and Cann, and making Cuts and Deviations by the Sides thereof, where necessary, to a certain Part of the said River Chelmer, above and near to a certain

Mill, called Beleigh Mill, near Maldon aforesaid, and by making a Navigable Canal from thence into the River Blackwater, and by widening, deepening, cleansing, and improving the said River Blackwater, and by making Cuts and Deviations by the Sides thereof, where necessary, to or near to H Mill, and by making a Canal from thence through the Village of Heybridge, to communicate with the said River Black-water, at, or nearly at, Colliers Reach aforesaid, Jbelow Maldon aforesaid; and that, if the said Navigation is carried from Beleigh Mill by Heybridge, as above described, it will be very prejudicial to the said Town and Port of Maldon, where there are several considerable Coal and other Wharfs established, and where much Traffic and Commerce is now carried on, which will be materially injured thereby; and that if, instead of the above-mentioned Part of the said Navigation from Beleigh Mill, a Cut or Canal navigable for Colliers, and other Vessels of large Burthen, be made from Collier's Reach to, or near to, the said Town and Port, and a Bason formed there, with proper Wharfs, Quays, and other Conveniencies thereto, and a Cut or Canal, navigable for Barges and other Vessels, made from the said Bason, to communicate with the said River Chelmer above Beleigh Mill aforesaid, the said Town and Port of Maldon will not receive any Injury, but will be considerably benefited, and the Variation in the Line will make the said Navigation equally convenient and commodious: And therefore praying, That Provision may be made in the said Bill for varying the Line of the said Navigation, as above described, in such Manner, and under such Regulations and Restrictions, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Sir John Jervis, Mr. Plu-mer, &c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

Ordered, That there be laid before this House, an Account of Account of all Imports and Exports into and from the e^p

Port of Maldon, in the County of Essex, from the 1st and from Day of January 1789 to the 31st Day of December 1792, Maldon,

distinguishing each Year. ordered.
