XXXII. ELG I Ni — Made by a Committee of Convention as Arbiters, in i 705, hnd ratified by the Convention, 8 July 1706.

Council consists of 14 Merchants and 3 Tradesmen, in all 17, including a Provost, 4 Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer. Elected thus:

The Old Council choose the New Council, and the Old and New Council choose the Magistrates out of their own Number; 3 Merchants and Two Deacons Trades Counsellors are chosen Yearly by the Council, irt the Room of the same Number put off; 7 Magistrates continue Counsellors after the Expiry of their Offices. The Convener is a Counsellor ex Officio; but it does not appear how he is elected.

The Council are obliged to put off 3 Merchants and 2 Tradesmen Yearly; but there is no Restriction against the Re-election of the other Counsellors, only the Baillies cannot be continued in their Offices above 2 Years; nor the Provost in his Office above 3 Years, without Intermission.

XXXIII. PEEBLES.

Council consists of a Provost, 2 Baillies, Dean of Guild, Treasurer, 11 Counsellors, and One Deacon; in all

17. Elected thus:

The Old Council choose the New, at a Head Court of the whole Burgesses, who are asked if they have any Complaint against any of them; and if any is made, it is then heard and discussed. Then the whole Magistrates and Council, having first supplied any Vacancies occasioned by Death, elect the New Council, and the Officers or Magistrates, out of Leets of 3 Persons for each, made by themselves, and without any Restriction against Re-election of either Counsellors or Magistrates. The Deacon, who is a Counsellor ex Officio, is elected out of a Leet of Six Persons made by the Trade, which is shortened to 3 by the Magistrates, of which 3 the Trade must elect One.

XXXIV. T A IN. — Appears to have been framed in 1708, in consequence of a Recommendation from Convention by a Committee of Convention and the Town Council. In 1730, the Convention allowed the Burgh to elect a 3d Baillie.

The Council consists of 15, including a Provost, 2 or 3 Baillies, a Treasurer, and Dean of Guild. Elected thus:

The Old Council choose the New Council, and out of the New Council elect the Magistrates. The Provost may be re-elected to his Office 3 Years, the Baillies 2 Years, without Intermission. There is no Restriction against the Re-election of the Old Counsellors into the New Council, except that Four Persons must be changed Yearly.

XXXV. CRA ILL. — 9th June 1711. The Council declare, that because heretofore there hath been no formal Sett, they find it just and reasonable that the Sett underwritten shall be punctually observed.

Council consists of 3 Bailies, a Treasurer, 11 Merchant and 6 Trades Counsellers; in all 21. Elected thus:

The Old Council choose Two Merchants and One Tradesman as New Counsellors. The 14 other Counsellors remain without Election, and the Magistrates are elected by the Old and New Council, and 7 Deacons of Trades.

No Provision as to changing any of the Council, except the Three above-mentioned; and the others may remain without Change, or be re-elected.

XXXVI. BANFF. — Dated 1709, and altered from former Sett in 1704, by the Authority of Town Council and Inhabitants, at a Head Court, because it changed the haill Council except and the haill Magistracy.

The Number of the Council is 17, without Distinction of Trades and Merchants, except the Deacon Convener and his Assessor Tradesmen, Elected thus:

XXXVII. FORFAR.

26 June 1710, The Council agreed, That the Sett following should be the Sett in all Time

coming.

The Council consists of a Provost, 2 Baillies, a Treasurer, 11 Merchant Counsellors, and Deacons; in all t 9. Elected thus:

The Old Council makes a Leet of 8 Persons for the Magistracy, and choose 15 New Counsellors, but who are not Yearly Counsellors; and these 15, with the Deacons elected by the Trades, along with the Old Magistrates and Council, elect the Provost, Baillies, and Treasurer for the ensuing Year, out of the Leets made by the Old Council; thereafter the New Council of 11 are elected by the Old Council.

The Magistrates may continue 2 or 3 Years. There is no Restriction against the Re-election of 11 of the Counsellors.

XXXVIII. ROTHS AY.

Council consists of a Provost, 2 Baillies, Treasurer, and Counsellors, Number not mentioned. Elected thus t

The Old Magistrates and Old Council choose of the Old Council, and One of the Old Magistrates, who choose the whole Council for the ensuing Year. The Old and New Council choose the Magistrates out of Leets.

No Limitation as to the Time of Re-election. The Officer warns the haill New Council, and does not warn if any be set off.

XXXIX. FO.

Council Consists of 17, including Provost, Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer. Elected thus:

Notice is given by Tuck (Beat) of Drum, to the whole Burgesses, Heritors, and Inhabitants, placading on the Cross, and other usual Advertisements. Then the Old Council chooses the New, and are changed Yearly as Occasion offers; the New Council chooses the Magistrates, and puts off or takes on, or continues them, as thd Circumstance of the Place requires.

It is certified in 1711, that the Sett has been unaltered for many Years.

No Provision against the Re-election of the same Counsellors or Magistrates.

XL. RUTHERGLEN.

It appears that the Magistrates, with the Consent of the Inhabitants, in 1671, because of Divisions on Account of the Practice of the Provost and Baillies, to elect and continue a Council by themselves, altered the Sett, and this Sett was altered again in 1710.

By the New Sett in 1671, the Council was to consist of 15 Counsellors, besides a Provost and Two Baillies, in all. Elected thus:

The Trades of Smiths, Weavers, and Taylors, give in a List of 6 each, in all 18, out of which the Provost and 2 Baillies shall choose Three Counsellors out of each; in all 9.

The 4th Trade of Taylors shall give a List of Persons, out of which the Provost and 2 Baillies shall choose Two Counsellors; and the remanent Burgesses and Inhabitants of the said Burgh and Territory, bearing Scotland Lot, shall give in a Leet of 8 Persons, out of which the said Provost and 2 Baillies shall choose Counsellors.

The Old Provost and Common Council, with 30 other additional Persons to be chosen by them, shall choose the Provost and 2 Baillies.

The Provost and Baillies must be changed Yearly, and cannot be continued; but there is no Limitation of Re-election of the other Counsellors. The Act of the Council, 1710, enacts that no Person shall be Provost who has not been One Year a Baillie; a Baillie who has not been One Year a Treasurer; or a Treasurer, or any of the other Magistrates, unless he be an ordinary Burgess, having his Residence therein, and 13 Scots of

Land belonging thereto, during his Office.

XLI. NORTH BERWICK.

The Sett says, the ancient Constitution preserved inviolable according to the Charter. The Charter, as returned, contains no Constitution nor Clause of Election.

The Council consists of 12. Elected thus:

The Old Council elect 2 New Counsellors for the next Year, and these 2, with (he Old Council, in all 14, elect 2 Baillies and a Treasurer, out of Leets of the Old Council made by themselves; thereafter the 14> or a* least a Quorum of 5 of the 14, reduce the remaining Counsellors by striking off 2 to 7, making the total Number 12.

33 Geo. III. 17° Junii.

No Limitation as to toe Time either Counsellors or Officers may continue in Council, only Two of toe Council must be changed Yearly.

XLII. CUL:

The Council consists of 3 Baillies, a Dean of Guild, a Treasurer, and 21 Counsellors; in all 26. Elected thus:

Each of the Old Council leets 2 Persons, and the whole Council chooses One of those 2 to be on the New Council till the Number be full; each of the 3 Baillies makes a List of Persons, out of which the 12 Baillies, Dean of Guild, Treasurer, and Council Old and New, choose 6, out of which 6 the 3 Magistrates are elected. Then the Dean of Guild and Treasurer make each Leets of Two; out of the First Leet the Dean of Guild is chosen, and out of the 2d Leet the Treasurer is chosen, by the whole Magistrates and Council.

There is no Limitation of Restriction against a Counsellor leering himself with another, or against his being re-elected as a new. Counsellor.

Nor is there any Restriction against the former Magistrates and Office Bearers being leeted and re-elected by the Council.

XLIII. LA UD ER. — Certified to the House of Commons, in 1788.

The Council consists of 15 Counsellors and Two Baillies, without Distinction of Merchants and Tradesmen; in all 17. Elected thus:

The whole Old Counsel make Choice of New Counsellors, then the Old Council, with those 4, making 21, make a Leet of any Counsellors with the 2 then Baillies, and those 6 being removed, the remaining 15 out of that Leet choose 2 Baillies; then each of these Baillies strikes out 2 from the List of the Old Council,' leaving of the Old Council 13, if the Baillies are re-elected, and if not, 11.

There is no Limitation against the Re-election of Baillies and Counsellors, only Four of the Counsel of the preceding Year must be changed, but there is no Restriction against changing the Four New Counsellors of the preceding Year, leaving the others as before.

XLIV. KILRE.

The Council consists of 3 Baillies, Treasurer, and 11 Burgesses, without Distinction of Merchants and Tradesmen; in all 15. Elected thus:

The Old Council elect the New Council; then the Baillies make out a Leet of Nine, of which they are always 3, and the Treasurer makes a Leet of 3 Persons, of which he is always One, and out of these Leets the Three Baillies and Treasurer of the ensuing Year are elected by the Votes of the Old Baillies, Council, and whole qualified Burgesses.

There is no Restriction against the Old Council re-electing themselves, that is 11 out of 15.

In the same Manner the Baillies and Treasurer may be re-elected out of Leets, but not by the Council alone, but by the Council and qualified Burgesses, so that Four may be changed Yearly.

XLV. ANNAN

23d June 1712. . The Magistrates and Council declare and ordain, that the following hath been, now is, and shall be the Sett of our Burgh in Time coming.

The Council consists of a Provost; Three Baillies, a Treasurer, a Dean, and 13 Counsellors, without Distinction of Merchants and Trades; in all 19. — The Mode of Election is not mentioned.

XLVI. SANQUHAR.

The Return states, that the Burgh had no Sett, and that in July 1713, the Convention'remitted to the Commissioners for Dumfries, Kirckudbright, Annan, and Lochmaben, to make a Sett for the Burgh, and report. The Sett they made, after considering* the Charters, is,

The Council to consist of a Provost, 3 Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer, with 11 Counsellors, Heritors, Merchants, and Tradesmen, Burgesses Residenters; in all 17. Elected thus:

The Old Council shall choose toe New; that none of toe Old Council shall continue longer than One Year,1 unless they be chosen again; and that Four at least shall be Annually changed. There is no Restriction against the Re-election of the remaining 13 Counsellors.

XLVII. NE1V GALLOWAY.

Is not dated. Returned to the House of Commons in 1788.

Recites, That by the Charter, 16th January 1629, Power is given to the Inhabitants of the Burgh, and Council and Community of the same for the Time, to elect Magistrates, and Counsellors, and Commissioners to Parliament, with Power to Provost, Baillies, and their Successors, to make and constitute Laws, Acts, and Statutes, for the Government of the Burgh.

That by immemorial Custom, the Council consists of a Provost, Two Bailies, a Dean of Guild, Treasurer, and 15 Counsellors, without any Distinction of Tradesmen and Merchants; in all 20. Elected thus:

The Provost names 3. and each of the Baillies One Counsellor; these 5 name One each, and these 2d 5 name One each; in all 15. The Counsellors then choose a Provost and 2 BaiHies, different from any elected into the Council. There is nothing said of the Election of Treasurer and Dean of Guild.

XLVIII. QUEENSFERRY. Decree by Convention, 17th July 1710*

The Council consists of 18 Counsellors, and 2 or 3 Deacons; in all 20 or 21, including Magistrates, whose Names are not mentioned, f- Seamen, -f Landsmen.

The Election is nearly unintelligible. — The ancient Custom is declared inviolably to be observed as to the Number of Electors; viz'. — The 18 Old Counsellors, and 14 Burgesses, Two or Three of the Deacons being of that Number, and those choose the Magistrates and Council, 2 or 3 Deacons beings always of the Council.

It does not appear how the Burgesses are chosen, for though there is a Poll at the Election 1710, yet in all Time thereafter it is declared that the Election shall be according to former old Custom, not explained.

In case of the Absence of any of the Council or warned Burgesses, Electors, the Magistrates and Council shall fill up the Vacancies, -f- Seamen, and Landsmen; and if not so many Seamen, Landmen to be allowed to supply their Places.

XLIX. K INTO RE.

The Council consists of 9, with the Magistrates, whose Names or Number is not mentioned. Elected thus:

The Old Council, consisting of Nine, with the Magistrates, choose new Magistrates, and then the Old Council, with the New Magistrates, choose the New Council.

There is no Restriction as to Re-election of the same Persons.

L. INVERURY.

The Sett, as delivered to Convention in 1710, is exactly the same with Kintore, without specifying the Magistrates. — But by a Sett, certified the ist of October 1788, to have been observed for 40 Years past, the Number of Magistrates is mentioned, being a Provost, 3 Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer, and 3 Counsellors; in all 9; all being Inhabitants, except that One or Two some Years may live some Distance, but must be Burgesses.

The Mode of Election is not specified by the new Sett, only the Magistrates order the Town Officer to advertize the Day of Election to the whole Citizens, that every Person concerned may appear at Court. In neither Sett is there any Restriction against Re-election.

LI. INVERBER

Certified, 1709, to have been and now to be the Custom.

The Council consists of a Provost, 2 Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer, and 9 Counsellors; in afll >5- -

The Old Council choose the 6 Magistrates, and the remaining 9 Counsellors. No Restriction as to Re-election.

LII. STRANRAER.

1711. The Council declare the following to have been the accustomed Sett

The Council consists of a Provost, 2 Baillies, and 15 Counsellors, including Dean of Guild and Treasurer; in all 18. Elected thus:

The Provost and 2 Baillies, or Two of them, divide the 15 Counsellors into Three Lists of 5 each, those 5 are removed per Vices, and the Remainder vote whether all or any of them shall be continued for the next Year; and if all or any are not continued, a like Number of Burgesses is immediately elected to make up the Number of 15 Counsellors. Then the Magistrates make a Leet of Three for the Provost, and Four of the Council for Baillies, out of which the Council elect the Provost and Baillies.

Then they elect which of the Counsellors they please the Dean of Guild and Treasurer.

The Provost is only continued Two Years.

There is no Restriction against the Continuance of the Council, the Vote being whether all or any of them shall be continued Counsellors or not.

LIII. WHITHORN.

The Council consists of a Provost, 2 Baillies, and 15 Counsellors; in all 18. Elected thus:

The Council changes Three of their Number every Year, and elect Three others in their Place; the other 15 Counsellors may be continued without Change.

Out of these 18 the whole New Council choose the Magistrates, who cannot continue in that Office above 2 Years.

There is no Restriction against the Re-election of Counsellors by themselves, except that 3 Persons must go out Report re-Yearly. specting the

No Distinction of Trades and Merchants: New Council does not mean new Counsellors, for 15 of the Old may be re-elected.

LIV. DINGWALL:

Appears to have been established in 1710. An Act and Sett of the Magistrates and Council concerted with the neighbouring Burrowes by Appointment of Convention is approved of by an Act of Council of that Date.

The Council consists of 15, including the Provost, 2 Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer, without Distinction of Trades and Merchants. Elected thus:

The Old Council choose the New Council of Resident Merchants, Tradesmen, or Heritors, and from this New Council the Old Council choose, out of Leets, the Provost, Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer, without being restricted to have the Old Magistrates on the Leets. The Baillies may be continued Five Years, the other Magistrates only Three Years, and shall be Counsellors the Year after the Expiry of their Offices. It is declared that no Person shall be a Magistrate till he has been Two Years a Counsellor, and that Two at least of the Council be changed every Year.

It appears that the Words New Council does not mean different Persons from the Old Counsellors, for only Two Counsellors must necessarily be changed every Year.

LY. SELKIRK:

No Date to the written Sett produced to the House of Commons.

.The CoundLconsi, sts of 33; viz. Two Baillies, One Dean of Guild, and One Treasurer, Two Old Baillies, Old Dean of Guild, and Old Treasurer, Five Deacons of Trades, and Five Colleagues, 10 Merchant Counsellors, and Five Trades Counsellors; in all«33. Elected thus:

The Old Magistrates are continued in Council without Election the Year after going out of Office; the Trades elect their 5 Deacons out of Leets shortened by Council, and 5 Colleagues apparently without Leets. The whole Council, with the New Deacons, elect the Magistrates. The whole Council elect 5 Trades Counsellors, and as many Merchant Counsellors as make the Number of the Council 33.

There is no Restriction as to Re-election. — This Sett differs entirely from the Sett sent the Convention in 1709, also produced, fry which it is said the whole Council and Magistrates were continued, and not chosen Yearly.

LVI. CULROSS:

Appears to have been framed by Act of Convention 1658. Council consists of 6 Trafficking Merchants, and 6 Seafaring Men or Inland Traders, 7 Trades Counsellors, of whom 5 are Deacons; in all 19. All of them chosen by the Old Council.

The 7 Deacons vote in the Election of Magistrates, but the Trades Counsellors cannot be both Trades Baillie and Deacon the same Year.

The Moderator of the Town Council to have Two Votes; it is not said by whom he is appointed.

No Limitation whatever of Re-election.

LVII. WICK:

Date of the Usage not mentioned. Burgh erected in 1589.

The Council, to consist of 10, including a Provost and Two Baillies,

By the Charter the Magistrates were to be chosen by the Advice of the Earl of Caithness, so that the constant Sett was to allow the Earl to be Provost and to choose one of the Baillies, and the Provost and Baillies to nominate 7 Counsellors; but now the Earl of Caithness not concerning himself with the Provostrie, the Town has been in use to chose their Provost and Baillies by the Plurality of the Poll, and the Provost and Baillies to nominate 7 Counsellors, with a Dean of Guild and Treasurer; in all 12.

LVIII. FORT ROSE:

Appears to have been made by the Magistrates in 1711, for regulating their Elections in Time coming.

Council consists of 15, including Provost, 3 Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer, without Distinction ot Merchants and Trades. Elected thus:

The whole Council elect the whole New Council without any Restriction, except that they must change at least Two of the Old Counsellors,' and elect Two New Counsellors in their Place.

The New Council to elect Magistrates from among themselves, who shall not continue more than 3 years. From-'' this it appears that New Council does not mean New Counsellors.

LIX. CAMPBELTON:

No Sett returned by Magistrates, but the Clause of Election in the Charter is in Appendix (A.) The Sett in the Books of Convention produced, directs that the Council shall consist of 17, including a Provost, Two Baillies, Dean of Guild, and Treasurer. Elected thus:

The Magistrates and Counsel elect new Counsellors in Place of of the old that are turned off; the Provost and Baillies are chosen by the Old and New Counsel out of Leets given by the Duke of Argylle. The Magistrates may be continued Two Years in Office, and the Baillies are Counsellors the Year after the Expiry of their Office; the Provost is a Counsellor for life. There is no other Restriction against Re-election but that Counsellors go off Yearly.

This Sett is not returned, but a Letter written by the Earl of Argylle, 1st June, 1700, appointing the Magistrates, and informing them, "We shall give you Instructions by the next to choyse your Commissioners " for the current Parliament."

LX. KIRKWALL:

Made by Act of Council for a particular Election, Year 1712, and to be in all Time thereafter as follows:

The Council shall consist of a Provost, Dean of Guild, 4 Baillies and Treasurer, and i6 Counsellors, of whom Deacons of Trades; in all 23. Elected thus:

The Council make a Leet of 2 of the Council, with foe present Provost, and of foe Council, with foe present Baillies, out of which the present Magistrates are elected by the Burgesses and Trades; each Burgess to have One Vote, and each Trade to have Two Votes by their Deacon or eldest Craftsman.

The Provost continues Two, and foe Baillies One Year, but both may be continued longer, if re-elected; then the Provost and Baillies so elected choose a Dean of Guild and Treasurer; then foe Provost and Baillies, Dean of Guild and Treasurer, choose foe New Council, but the Magistrates changed continue Counsellors. The Magistrates and Council, out of a Leet of Two, with foe old Deacon given in by each Craft, elect their respective Deacons.

No Limitation of Re-election of any Kind. The Provost and Baillies are chosen by foe Burgesses and Trades out of Leets of foe Council made by foe Council; and the Persons so chosen have the substantial Power of choosing foe New Council.

EXTRACT of Part of the Commission of King Charles II. 16th June 1684.

Nosq; intelligentes quod in pluribus Regalibus nostris Burgis bonum publicum reditus et patrimonium a Magistratibus pro tempore aut profuse dilapidantur aut privatim decoqtiuntur et plerumq; in fines et usus prorsus alios quam per leges applicari ordinantur aut quam per benignas donationes nostras nostrorumve illus-trissimorum progenitorum destinata et allocata fuere, applicantur; speciatim vero quod Regalia nostra burga, absq; ulla necessitate debita contraxerunt, et postquam donationes et concessiones a nobis nostrisque predeces-soribus ad Debita ilia persolvenda omnino sufficientes obtinuere, et postquam et Civium consensu onera ad dicta debita persolvenda sunt imposita, nihilominus eadem debita majori ex parte in plurimis nostris burgis, insoluta remanent, atque reditus emolumenta et proficua, a publico bono Burgi amplissimis et benignis nostris donationibus, et civium liberis suffragiis, et consensu exsurgentia, magnopere consumuntur et indebite applicantur, unde non solum murmura et querimonias quam plurime in Burgis oriuntur, verum etiam illi qui magis suo lucro et emolumento privato quam Burgi commodo,. munerique et officio Magistratus con-sulunt factiones et divisiones in Burgo movere inducuntur, ut se-ipsos ad officium Magistratus elegi procu-rent, utque ipsi eorumque amici, propinqui et Clientes in dicto officio continuentur, ut inde occasionem habeant bonum publicum reditusque burgi consumendi in praemiis ad amicos suos et Burgi factiones conti* nuandos. Qui vero si stride Rationem reddere cogerentur de bono publico red iti bus et patrimonio burgi, et ut eadem necessarie et utiliter applicata fuere in communibus burgi comodis et negotiis, probare tene-rentur, proque dilapidatis et indebite applicatis, Rationem Reddere cogerentur, eaque Burgo presolvere et rependere decemerentur ac aliter pro prava sua Administratione prout requiru'nt Leges Regni Mulctarentur et punirentur praedicta ilia Mala maximopere prevenirentur et Mederentur; atque inde Murmura, queremoniae, et contentiones pro officio Magistratus restringentur et Sedarentur, atque mercatores, opitices, aliique cives dictorum Burgorum diligentur et quiete artes et vocationes suas prosequerentur et burga nostra bene et pacifice Gubernarentur, &c.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That such a Number of Copies of the said Report, with the Appendix thereunto, be printed, as shall be sufficient for the Use of the Members of the House.

A Motion was made, and the Question being put, That this House will, early in the next Session of Parliament, take into Consideration the State of the Royal Burghs in Scotland;

It passed in the Negative.

And then the House adjourned till Wednesday Morning next, Ten of the Clock.

His Majesty's After which, His Majesty was pleased to make a peecmost Gracious Speech from the Throne, to both Houses of Parliament, as followeth; viz.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

The Firmness, Wisdom, and Public Spirit, by which your Conduct has been eminently distinguished on the many important Occasions which have arisen during the present Session, demand My peculiar Acknowledgments.

Your firm Determination to support the Established Constitution, and the zealous and general Concurrence in that Sentiment, which My Subjects have so strongly and seasonably manifested, could not fail to check every Attempt to disturb the internal Repose of these Kingdoms; and you will, I doubt not, in your several Counties, encourage the Continuance of the same vigilant Attention to that important Object.

The rapid and signal Successes which, in an early Period of the Campaign, have attended the Operations of the Combined Armies; the respectable and powerful Force which you have enabled Me to employ by Sea and Land; and the Measures which I have concerted with other Powers for the effectual Prosecution of the War, afford the best Prospect of a happy Issue to the important Contest in which we are engaged: — It is only by Perseverance in vigorous Exertions, and by endeavounng to improve the Ad-

vantages already acquired, that we can hope to obtain the great End to which My Views are uniformly directed, the Restoration of Peace on such Terms as may be consistent with our permanent Security, and with the general Tranquillity of Europe.

Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

I return, you My particular Thanks for the Chear-fulness and Dispatch with which you have granted the necessary Supplies; and I am happy to reflect, that you have been enabled liberally to provide for the Exigencies of the Public Service in a Manner so little burthensome to My People.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

The Arrangements which you have formed for the Government of the British Territories in India, and for the Regulation of Our Commerce with that Part of the World, will, I doubt not, secure and augment the important Benefits which we have already derived from those valuable Possessions. It has been impossible for Me to see, without Concern, the Embarrassment which has lately arisen in the State of Commercial Credit; but the Steps which you have taken to prevent the Progress of that Evil appear already to have been productive of very salutary Consequences; and while they have afforded a striking Instance of your Attention to the Interests of My People, their Effect has furnished additional reason to believe that the Distress, which has been felt, proceeded from a Concurrence of temporary Causes, and not from any Diminution of the real Wealth, or any Failure in the permanent Resources of the Country.

I have much Satisfaction in reflecting on the effectual Protection which I have been enabled to afford to the Trade of My Subjects since the breaking out of the War; I am at the same Time persuaded that, if Our Commercial Interests had unavoidably been affected to a more considerable Extent, it would not have been forgotten that We are contending for Our future Security, and for the permanent Preservation of Advantages, the, most striking and the most valuable, which any Nation has ever, by the Blessing of Providence, been permitted to enjoy.

And afterwards the Lord Chancellor, by His Majesty's Parliament Command, said, prorogued.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

It is His Majesty's Royal Will and Pleasure, that this Parliament be prorogued to Tuesday, the 13th Day of August next, to be then here holden; and his Parliament is accordingly prorogued to 1 he

] 3th Day of August next.
